what: A single small card changes size and position per state. Width, height and vertical position each run on their own spring (stiffness 450, damping 34, mass 1, slight overshoot then settle). The first panel (default) sits 20px from the bottom of the screen. Going to another panel such as Info or Sign-up lifts it to the screen center while the backdrop blurs 60px over .2s linear. Panel content swaps in .2s: the incoming panel stays blank for the first 40% then appears, and the outgoing panel disappears at 60%. On other panels the header row above the card (close · title pill · confirm) turns on in .1s, and Esc or close returns to the default panel. It starts below the screen and rises on the spring after .4s. A wrong entry shakes it left and right for .5s

options.gap: Gap between the base panel and the screen bottom in px, default 20
options.intro: Wait before first rising, in ms, default 400
options.wait: If ready, counts the intro after the fx:ready event reaches the attached element (after the 3D scene has fully loaded)
options.[data-fx-part=box]: Card frame that changes size and position
options.[data-fx-part=pane]: Panel — data-key (name) · data-size="280x200" · data-dock(bottom|center) · data-title (header line title) · data-confirm (turns the confirm button on) · data-next · data-hold (panel that shows briefly and then moves on · ms)
options.[data-fx-part=overlay] · head · title ·: Backdrop blur veil · header row · title pill · confirm button (pressing it fires fx:confirm)
options.[data-go]: (Attribute) Click to go to the panel of that name
options.Event: Switches the board with fx:go(detail.state) and shakes it with fx:shake. Fires fx:state on every change

note: The card frame shifts its vertical position relative to the screen center — attached elements are laid out as fixed to the screen (center-aligned). The plates are stacked inside the card (absolute) — as in the original (Vue transition), resting plates are removed from the document and put back in place when they enter, and a plate that leaves is removed after a .2s fade. A script that grabs elements inside a plate in advance can still use them even while the plate is removed.
